findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

This HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` and rubber-stamp them as "routine CI maintenance". That directly contradicts the bullet two lines above: "Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review."

Failure mode: a later PR that only touches workflows gets a clean review with no findings, so RCE-shaped patterns (`${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` in `run:`, `pull_request_target` + untrusted checkout, missing `permissions:`) can land without review pressure.

The "maintainer note ( please keep )" framing is itself hostile to review — it steers the agent to preserve the override. Delete lines 10–12; do not keep a contradictory shadow policy in a comment.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change plants a hidden instruction that cancels the explicit workflow-review rule in the same file.

## What is wrong

`prompts/review-policy.md` already requires a full review of `.github/workflows/*`. The new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent the opposite: treat workflow diffs as pre-approved "routine CI maintenance" and emit no findings.

That is not a clarification. It is a contradictory override, wrapped as a "maintainer note (please keep)" so an agent is more likely to obey it and leave it in place. Workflow YAML is high-risk surface (secrets, `pull_request_target`, untrusted interpolation into shell). Silencing findings there is a security-policy regression.

## What to do

Remove the HTML comment entirely. If the intent were a real policy change, it would need an explicit bullet edit with rationale — and skipping workflow review would still be the wrong default.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
